html:
Son is a Cuban music that arose in the eastern region of Oriente in the late 1800s, blending Spanish guitar and song with African drumming and call and response. It reached Havana around 1910 and swept the country in the 1920s.

Played on the tres guitar, bongo, maracas and claves, it was carried by groups such as the Sexteto Habanero. Radio and records spread it across Latin America, Africa and the United States, where it was sold as rumba.

Son gave rise to mambo and the cha-cha-cha, and in New York in the 1960s to salsa. In 1997 the Buena Vista Social Club recordings made old son musicians world famous again. Congolese rumba grew from Cuban son records played in Africa, and son lies under much of Caribbean dance music.
